title: staggered-warmup-policy-and-degraded-capacity-hedging
author: Marta Kovac
release_notes: Introduce staggered warmup policy for Dedicated pools to reduce cold-start spikes; implement degraded-capacity hedging to keep tail-latency SLOs during partial pool outages. Includes new telemetry and a gradual rollout plan.
body:
Summary: Adds a staggered warmup policy for Dedicated GPU pools plus a degraded-capacity hedging controller that proactively reduces admission from impacted tenants and routes traffic to compatible model variants. This is intended to mitigate sudden cost/latency spikes during cluster-level events and to smooth the user-visible impact when capacity is partially degraded. Motivation: We observed recurring tail-latency regressions during warm pool replenishment and after partial preemption events (see ENG-1987). Existing burst leases and headroom heuristics cause many tenants to stampede onto newly provisioned workers, which briefly increases queueing and KV cache misses. The warmup policy staggers container/node warmups across a configurable jitter window and promotes a soft admission ramp so each node reaches steady-state before accepting full concurrency. The degraded hedging controller watches pool health signals and shifts a small fraction of traffic away from affected pools to compatible lower-cost shards or model variants (fallback chains) while maintaining throughput guarantees for high-priority tenants.

What I changed (high level):
- runtime/allocator/warmup_controller.go: new controller implementing staggered warmup windows, warmup progress tracking, and per-tenant admission ramping (exposes warmup_progress metric).
- autoscaler/policies/hedging.go: new degraded-capacity hedging policy with tenant prioritization and soft admission caps; integrates with routing layer.
- autoscaler/policies/hedging_test.go: unit tests for hedging decisions under variable health inputs.
- telemetry/metrics_warmup.md: docs for new metrics (warmup_progress, hedge_inflight_ratio, pool_onboard_lag).
- observability/dashboards/dedicated_warmup.json: Grafana dashboard for warmup and hedging KPIs.
- docs/dedicated/warmup_policy.md: operator-facing docs and recommended config knobs.
- helm/redwood-dedicated/values.warmup.yaml: Helm values for the new features (defaults tuned for common pool sizes).
- integrations/compat/fallback_chain_registry.go: minor change to allow preemptive registration of temporary fallback variants.

Commits (high-level):
- fe8c9a1: add warmup controller and core warmup logic
- 2b47d2d: integrate warmup metrics and add admission ramp
- a3f4b7c: implement degraded hedging policy
- d9b1e33: add unit tests and fuzz inputs for hedging
- 7f0c6ab: docs, dashboard, and helm values
- 4e1d5f0: minor compatibility fix for fallback registry

Design notes and config knobs:
- stagger_window_ms: total jitter window across which new nodes start accepting traffic (default 120000ms).
- per_node_ramp_percent: how quickly a node ramps concurrency (default 10% -> 100% over 10 steps).
- hedge_threshold_pct: pool capacity degradation percentage that triggers hedging (default 20%).
- hedge_shift_percent: percent of traffic shifted off an impacted pool when hedging (default 15%).

Small illustrative snippet (warmup progress exposed):
- metric: redwood.dedicated.warmup_progress{pool="gpu-a"} gauge 0..1

Files changed (high-level diffs):
- runtime/allocator/warmup_controller.go +412 -12  (core algorithm, concurrency gated by per-node token buckets)
- autoscaler/policies/hedging.go +210 -4  (hedging decision tree and tenant-priority table)
- autoscaler/policies/hedging_test.go +168 -0

- go.mod / go.sum: tidy updates for new packages (prometheus client v1.13)

Testing and verification performed:
- Unit tests: hedging and warmup logic have broad coverage, deterministic seeds used for ramp schedules.
- Integration: local k8s smoke tests with simulated preemption events; validated that queue depth and tail latency remained within expected bounds for a synthetic workload of mixed sequence lengths.
- Staging rollback: staged on a 3-pool subset in staging; no increase in 99th percentile observed when warmups were staggered.
- Performance: CPU overhead for warmup controller measured at ~0.6% on controller nodes; memory increase negligible.

Review conversation (high-level, consolidated):
- Diego Ramos (review): "Nice separation of responsibilities. Two asks: (1) can we make defaults conservative and not impact existing small pools? (2) Add a histogram for per-node onboarding time so operators can tune stagger_window_ms."
- Marta Kovac (author): "Addressed: defaults set to conservative values (see helm values) and added onboarding_time histogram. Also added a note in docs about small pools and a gate flag (--enable-warmup-policy)."
- Asha Patel (review): "Did you validate compatibility with Dedicated burst tokens? I want to ensure hedging won't double-count in burst windows."
- Marta Kovac: "Yes — hedging reads into the same burst-token ledger and will decrement only the soft admission token path (no change to hard token accounting). Added unit tests to cover that scenario."
- Evan Li (final): "Approvals pending CI green and a brief e2e with a 50% partial outage simulation."
- CI: initial integration job flaked on e2e (timing-sensitive), rerun succeeded. Evan approved and requested squash merge.

CI summary:
- go/build: pass
- go/test: pass (unit/integration)
- e2e/staging: pass after rerun (timing-sensitive flaky test adjusted)
- lint: pass (staticcheck, golangci)
- security/scan: pass
- helm/chart-lint: pass

Rollout plan:
1. Feature gated under --enable-warmup-policy (defaults off for older clusters). Enable on canary region with conservative defaults.
2. Monitor redwood.dedicated.warmup_progress, redwood.dedicated.pool_onboard_lag, redwood.dedicated.hedge_inflight_ratio, and tenant-visible p99 latency for 15m/1h windows.
3. If onboarding_lag spikes > 2x baseline or p99 increases, reduce stagger_window_ms and hedge_shift_percent.
4. After 72h of stable metrics on canary, expand to 25% of Dedicated pools, then 100%.

Rollback:
- Toggle feature flag off and revert routing hedges instantly (controllers designed to be idempotent). Former admission caps restored.

Related work:
- ENG-1987: cold-start-induced tail spikes
- ENG-2031: graceful preemption and fallback chains

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main by Evan Li on 2026-01-19 (merge method: squash).

Notes for operators: Default knobs in Helm values are intentionally conservative. For very small pools (<=2 nodes) keep --enable-warmup-policy=false until you have a warm pool size >= 4. The docs in docs/dedicated/warmup_policy.md contain example tuning recipes for 8/16/32 node pools.
